title: Why Sodium Explodes in Water: The Textbook's Missing Answer
summary: A translation of the same day's science episode. Textbooks say a lump of sodium explodes in water because of the heat and the hydrogen gas the reaction makes. The episode shows why that answer is incomplete. In two thousand fifteen, high-speed cameras filmed drops of sodium-potassium alloy and found that within the first millisecond electrons flood out of the metal into the water.
